item.title: Re: class safe human clown doesn't fit with the scp universe
item.content:encoded:
Firstly, it's safe class because it's an animated television program, not an actual serial killer, which can be easily turned off and replaced with another program. Secondly, never does it imply that Bobble is a human, as it's an animated clown, and even if it was a human, humans can be SCPs because they're just regular humans with anomalous aspects. I have no problem if you dislike something, but you should dislike it for actual reasons.

EDIT: Seeing as you edited your comment, I guess I'll edit mine as well. Again, it's fine to not like something, but it should be for actual reasons. If you think it doesn't "fit in", then that's fine. I do object that this SCP is receiving "so much hate". If anything, it's highly beloved. If you're going to state your opinion on something, please read the whole article before doing so.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
So, I understand that this has been talked about in this comment section as well as the literal behind the scenes page for this skip, but I seriously have to recommend this be reclassified as Euclid. The process now seems to basically be extrapolating and assuming that whatever frequency or process is being used is never going to change.

The behind-the-scenes file actually proves against this, however. We know that Bobble has been around for centuries now, constantly changing its format and medium as to find the best way to manipulate its viewer. This, combined with the fact that it was able to interrupt its own broadcast and change it for an unspecified amount of time, makes me believe (and wonder why it hasn't) that it is able to adapt and assume any sort of new form of media as need be. If this is true 993 would, and should be able to, let's say, start it's own 24/7 livestream on Twitch. If it found its way onto the internet, I feel like the 05 would be taking this much more seriously.

Of course, I'm not really sure if that little correlation actually interferes with classification, but I still move that this needs to be looked at may be a little more closely. I definitely don't think that it needs to be reclassified as Keter though.
